title: intent group (set, show, advance, clear) -- first group through the dispatch seam
action: Port the intent group end to end: lib logic into a new crates/bee-core/src/intent.rs, CLI handlers (packages/bee/bee.mjs:4059-4134 (REVIEW-CORRECTED range — the block closes at 4134, not 4132)) into the queen-bee group registered behind the rpl-1 seam. Store is one JSON file per sanitized key at .bee/intent/<key>.json (intent.mjs:52,69-70) -- NOT jsonl. Preserve exactly: writeJsonAtomic read-modify-write with no lock (intent.mjs:216,238); advanceIntent structurally able to touch only next_action (the design invariant at intent.mjs:23-24); fail-open reads where a missing or corrupt anchor never throws (intent.mjs:25-28); the NO_WORK_PHASES predicate (idle, compounding-complete) resolved by reading state via bee-core::state, matching intent.mjs:33,49. Key sanitization must match byte-for-byte including its behavior on empty, unicode, path-separator and traversal-shaped keys. VALIDATION-FOUND OBLIGATION (feasibility matrix row 7): crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs today writes NO intent store -- it contains zero references to `intent` (verified by grep during validation). Extend fixture::generate to seed .bee/intent/ with several keys, at least one of them unicode and one long, BEFORE writing the scenarios; without this every intent scenario would diff two empty directories and report a meaningless clean. Register --cmd-check scenarios covering: every verb on an absent store; set then show round-trip; advance on a missing anchor; clear on an absent key; a traversal-shaped key; a corrupt anchor file fed to both show and advance; and NO_WORK_PHASES both true and false. REVIEW-FOUND TRAP, named so it is not rediscovered the hard way: sanitizeIntentKey ends in .slice(0, 120) (packages/bee/lib/intent.mjs:66) and JS slice counts UTF-16 CODE UNITS. Rust &s[..120] counts bytes and .chars().take(120) counts scalar values; all three disagree on non-ASCII, and the JS form can split a surrogate pair mid-character. Port the code-unit semantics exactly, and put in the scenarios a key longer than 120 code units, a key whose 120th boundary falls inside a surrogate pair, and an astral-plane key. Also assert this group's own unknown-verb usage fallback line (packages/bee/bee.mjs:6586-6609).

truths: crates/queen-bench/src/fixture.rs seeds a non-empty .bee/intent/ store, proven by the generator's own output listing the seeded keys
cargo run --release --manifest-path crates/Cargo.toml -p bee-parity -- --cmd-check --group intent reports every intent scenario clean, mjs vs queen-bee, over that non-empty fixture
the negative control fires on every intent scenario
a traversal-shaped key produces byte-identical output and byte-identical on-disk paths in both runtimes
a corrupt anchor file makes neither runtime throw on show, and both behave identically on advance
a key longer than 120 UTF-16 code units, a key whose 120th boundary splits a surrogate pair, and an astral-plane key all sanitize byte-identically to mjs
the intent unknown-verb usage fallback line is byte-identical to mjs

trace.outcome: intent group (set/show/advance/clear) ported end to end behind the rpl-1 seam: bee-core/src/intent.rs (UTF-16-code-unit sanitizer, per-key atomic write, fail-open read, next_action-only advance), queen-bee/src/ledger/ handlers, queen-bench fixture now seeds a 5-key .bee/intent/ store with a pinned floor, and 24 --cmd-check scenarios run mjs vs queen-bee with a per-scenario negative control that fires on the declared channel. The last red was a real harness finding, not a flake: the surrogate-pair scenario aimed its mutation at .bee/intent/<119 a's>-.json, the key the runtimes PRINT, while the anchor is stored at <119 a's>.json because intentPath re-sanitizes an already-sanitized key and /-+$/ eats the dash the 120-code-unit cut exposed. Mutation corrected onto the path the write actually reads, plus a unit test pinning the printed-key/on-disk-name divergence. Port parity was never in question: mjs and queen-bee wrote byte-identical paths throughout.
